newsitem.title: UK: BOC chief positive on '97 business growth.
newsitem.headline: BOC chief positive on '97 business growth.

text.p: British Chemicals firm BOC Group Plc said it expected to continue making progress in its gases and distribution services business in 1997 but could be under pressure from the strength of sterling.

"While these exchange rate movements make it difficult to predict the year's profit, we expect 1997 to be a year of solid underlying progress," Danny Rosenkranz, chief executive of the BOC group told shareholders at the firm's annual meeting.
Rosenkranz predicted the current year would be "somewhat less dynamic" for its vacuum business as it worked its way through the down-turn in the semi-conductor industry.
He said the firm expected a recovery in its health care business.
Rosenkranz said the group's capital investment in its gas business during the year was likely to exceed the 631 million stg that it pumped into the business in 1996.
BOC's healthcare business, mainly driven by Ohmeda, is on the verge of recovery, he said.
The Ohmeda health division had been hit by continued falls in the price of BOC's once top-selling anaesthetic gas Forane and weak demand for anaesthetic machinery in the U.S.
The division's operating profit for the 12 months to September 1996 dropped 11 percent to 53.1 million stg.
"Our health care business should start to turn the corner towards the back end of this year, and next year move towards more satisfactory levels of profitability," Rosenkranz said.
